title: anime pipeline
status_note: Lab piece. The pipeline runs end to end on one card, but the series itself is pre-production: stills, storyboards and short test clips, no finished episode.
oneliner: Gray-box Blender previz in, anime frames and clips out, on one GPU.
role: I built the whole local pipeline and am using it to develop an original series, Meguri: the Blender previz scenes, the ComfyUI and video workflows, the storyboard boards, and the character looks.

spec.label: GB VRAM ceiling
spec.source: AGENTS.md memory budget: nothing may need more than 12 GB of VRAM (one RTX 3060)

body: I can block a shot as gray boxes in Blender and get an anime frame back that keeps the same camera, stairs and figure placement. The hero image is one frame both ways; the loop is the same idea in motion.

The pipeline is Blender previz, then ComfyUI and a video model steered by depth and line passes, all on one 12 GB RTX 3060. Nothing is allowed to need more than 12 GB of VRAM, so I lean on 8-bit weights and tiled decode. Every generation is appended to a run log.

The test bed is an original series, Meguri, with two shows in development, SHUTO and SURI. I storyboard in previz first and only spend GPU time on video once a board is approved. Look Lab pages compare print styles on the same frames.

What I learned: depth is the operator. Once the previz carries the camera and layout, the style becomes a setting I can change, and most failures are about the model ignoring the scene rather than the scene being wrong. This is still a lab; the character consistency and shot-to-shot continuity are not solved.
